properties.summary: Administrative violation issued on 7/24/2023 to ALLSHOUSE TERRENCE L JR in Pleasant Township, Warren county. OGA3211(H) - WELL PERMITS - LABELING - Failure to install, in a permanent manner, the permit number on a completed well.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: ALLSHOUSE TERRENCE L JR
Violation Type: Administrative
Violation Date: 7/24/2023
Violation Code: OGA3211(H) - WELL PERMITS - LABELING - Failure to install, in a permanent manner, the permit number on a completed well.
Violation ID: 8153663
Permit API: 123-42082
Unconventional: No
County: Warren
Municipality: Pleasant Township
Inspection Type: Complaint Inspection
Inspection Date: 7/24/2023
Comments: This well was inspected as part of an on going stray gas migration case involving gas migrating into a private water supply (CTS#373559). The well head and casing strings were observed at the time of inspection for leaks, deterioration, corrosion, and possible failures. As part of the investigation 3 slam bar holes were placed into the ground approximately 1-2 feet from the well head to identify if any methane was migrating from the well-bore. All valves were open and the well is currently equipped for production. 2 check valves were in place on the production lines and were oriented correctly. Well records, production reports, and mechanical integrity assessment reports were reviewed to assist in the investigation. NO methane was detected in the slam bar holes utilizing a MSA ALTAIR 5X meter which was calibrated on 07/17/2023. No casing string pressures were observed at the time of inspection due to no pressure gauges in place and no operator provided well tender available. This well was labeled with an incorrect well API#, this issue was brought to the attention of the operator and promptly fixed. Further inspections of this well may be warranted to determine the root cause of the complaint.

Comments: On May 10, 2024, the Department conducted a FUI in Fayette County, Springfield Township on the MAWC 7020 Pad for a complaint received on April 11 2024 at 2:53. Accompanying in today's inspection was a MACW representative (Duane Goodsell) and Don Supcoe (Stone Ridge Energy). At the time of this inspection, the 1H and 3H wells were reported to be plugged with no monument present. The Act 9 sign was at the entrance of the access road. The ERP and PPC Plan were onsite at the time of this inspection. The access road appears to stabilized with no signs of erosion or sedimentation issues. No accelerated erosion or sedimentation issues were observed during this inspection. In the center of the pad near the location of reportedly plugged wells were previouslytwo stains that were oily in nature thatwere approximately 2ft by 2ft in size. The gravel has been removed from the two stained areas and the visually impacted materials placed into 5 gallon storage containers on-site. The Department recommended that the Operator remediate the areas as necessary in accordance with 78a66. It appears that the well site has yet to be restored. The Department recommends that the operator regrade, seed, and mulch site to obtain 70% uniform and adequate vegetative growth and restore the well site. The completion of plugging for this well reportedly occurred 12/27/2023, therefore the Operator is in compliance with the COA issued on 12/16/2021. The Operator has 9 months from plugging to complete a restoration of the former well site. Discussion between MAWC and the Operator(Stone Ridge Energy) had taken place onsite about restoration efforts of the site during this inspection. Based on today's inspection, violations shall remain outstanding at this time. Violations are outstanding, but are listed as new in this inspection report due to an app error.

Comments: On September 19, 2024, the Department conducted a Follow Up Inspection of Mountain View's George A Willlaims 4 well located in South Huntington Township, Westmoreland County in response to IR 3726379 where violations were issued for a spill from the production tank. A Notice of Violation response was received by the Department on May 16, 2024.At the time of this inspection, the access road which is off of a residential home's driveway appears stabilized with no erosion or sedimentation issues observed and the well site is located in a field adjacent to the residence home. The production tank that was leaking during IR 3726379 appears to be removed from the well site and the area where it sat appears to be the only area of the well site that is lacking 70% uniform and adequate vegetative growth. A well tag is fixed to the wellhead with all required information posted on it and no fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed coming from or near the well head. Production equipment on site appears to be heavily rusted, the Department recommends the Operator monitor and maintain the production equipment to ensure corrosion does not worsen and compromise the structural integrity.A background soil conductivity reading was taken in some vegetation up slope of the well site (0.1781 mS) and then several soil conductivity readings were taken in the area where the production tank once sat (0.562 mS, 0.718 mS, 0.1278 mS, 0.229 mS, 0.582 mS, 0.539 mS, 0.1788 mS, 0.619 mS, and 0.1467 mS). Some of the conductivity readings are elevated compared to the background reading while some readings in the same soil type are not elevated and are comparable to the background reading, subjugating that the issue is not the type of soil in this area, but that some of the contaminated soil has not yet been removed from the well site.The Department is recommending the Operator remove the remaining contaminated soil, dispose of it properly and replace it with fresh topsoil as well as seed and mulch to bring the entire site up to 70% uniform and adequate vegetative growth. Based on today's inspection, violations issue during IR 3726379 shall remain outstanding at this time.

Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 12/22/2025
Comments: This inspection occurred in response to a phone call made by Dan McCamey, of Minard Run Oil Company (MROC) on December 22, 2025. The purpose of the phone call was to report an incident which had occurred at Warrant 5107 Well #25P (API# 053-26767). A failure in the buried steel pipeline leading to this well resulted in leaking crude oil rising to the surface. A well tender spotted the crude oil earlier today and notified MROC immediately. A work crew arrived soon thereafter to repair the line, install containment, and begin remediating the released crude oil. Upon my arrival to the site, the pipeline had been repaired which stopped the release. The released crude oil had migrated down the road ditch for approximately 20 feet, across the road through a culvert, flowing downhill into a spring, ultimately entering Guiton Run (HQ-CWF) at (41.513992, -79.18582) after traveling approximately 50 yards. Pockets of weathered crude oil and emulsion were evident downstream for approximately 475 yards ending at (41.512156, -79.189991). The amount of crude oil released as a result of this incident was unknown due to the lack of accumulated product at the site. At this time, it is estimated that less than one barrel of product was released. A siphon dam was installed in the road ditch, beyond the direction of flow where the crude oil was initially spotted. A second siphon dam was installed and lined beyond the road culvert. Booms and diapers were already placed on the surface and at the point of entry in Guiton Run. Booms and diapers should be regularly monitored and replaced as necessary until the site is deemed remediated. Additional booms and diapers should be placed in Guiton Run to absorb and capture any released crude oil within the stream. The stream should be continuously monitored until there is no longer any evidence of crude oil. Follow up inspections will routinely be conducted to monitor remediation of this release. Confirmatory field screening and/or sampling will need to be conducted to verfiy that the cleanup is deemed complete prior to any seeding/mulching. The Department's Policy 800-5000-001- "Addressing Spills and Releases at Oil and Gas Well Sites or Access Roads" sets forth the procedure to be followed to resolve the violations associated with the spill/discharge/release documented in this Notice of Violation ("NOV"), by using either the Act 2 or the Alternative Remediation Process. The conventional well was equipped for production with a pump jack. The well name, API number, and operator information were displayed on a sign attached to the pump jack.

Comments: On February 4, 2026, the Department conducted an incident inspection at the Aphrodite Well Site (ESCGP issued on 5/9/2020, amended on 2/5/2024, expiring on 2/4/2029) in regards to a release reported to the Department on 2/3/2026 (CTS 394941). Present during the inspection was operator representative Jim Noon.According to Mr.Noon, this release is a seperate release, unrelated to the release documented in inspection report 4125373.The findings are as follows:At the time of the inspections, the Act 9 sign was present and appeared to be installed in accordance with 78a55. The Emergency Response Plan (ERP), Preparedness, Prevention and Contingency (PPC) plan (which contained all required components) and site plans were present in the onsite mailbox. The access road appeared stabilized with gravel.At the time of inspection, there are 5 total wells on the well pad. According to the operator, stimulation for all 5 wells has been completed and they are continuing to install production equipment in order to get the wells into active production.During the inspection, Mr. Noon guided the Department to the location of the reported release. According to Mr. Noon the release was discovered on 2/3/2026 when containment for drilling/stimulation equipment was being removed from the site. He stated that upon removal of the containment, staining was observed and after further assessment it was identified as a release of impaired water and reported to the Department. At the time of the inspection the operator is unsure of the total volume of impaired water that was released.The Department observed the location of the spill and remediation. It appeared the area of the release and ongoing remediation was in an approximate 40-foot by 80-foot area adjacent to the well heads near the entrance of the well pad.Mr. Noon stated that 2 small temporary sumps were excavated in the area of the release in order to isolate the release. The water collected in the sumps were being pumped out by a vacuum truck. Mr. Noon stated that 2 roll-off boxes had already been filled with impacted material, and they were waiting for additional boxes to continue remediation.Conductivity readings of 18.08mS, and 6.13mS were obtained in the 2 excavated sumps. Conductivity readings of 3.97mS, 1.25mS, 1.17mS, and 0.69mS were obtained in the area of the release/remediation.The Department requests the operator provide a copy of the secondary containment inspection records from January 1, 2026, through the date the secondary containment was removed, within 3 days of receiving this inspection report.The operator is also requested to submit a written response within seven (7) days of the receipt of this report. This written response should include an incident report, a timeline of remedial measures, and plan for remediation of the spill or release. The Department is requesting how the operator quantified the amount spilled. The Department also requests the waste manifest from the site remediation be submitted upon receipt.If the quantity of the spill is determined to be greater than 1 barrel (42 gallons),the operator will need to perform remediation in accordance with the Act 2 guidelines as set by 78a.66(c)(2).Based on today's inspection, violations are being issued against the Aphrodite 2M well for the observed release. Additional violations may be forthcoming pending receipt and review of the requested information/documentation.

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: EQT ARO LLC

Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 991491
Permit API: 081-21846
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: Cascade Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 4/13/2023
Comments: On April 13, 2023, DEP representative Brad Kline conducted an incident response to a reported spill at the EQT ARO LLC Chapman Bohlin Pad A. The spill of triethylene glycol and production fluid was reported to DEP by Zac Subra from a failed gasket on a reboiler at one of dehydration units onsite. Mr. Subra estimated about 42 gallons spilled outside of containment onto the well pad surface. DEP met with Mr. Subra and Penn E and R who was overseeing the clean up onsite. EQT contractors were just beginning to excavate the area of impact. The area of impact was about 20 ft. x 15 ft. on the southwest side of the dehydration unit. An additional area of impact under the reboiler was visually stained about 4 ft. x 2 ft. The well pad surface was visually impacted and the area had elevated conductivity in the 2,000 uS/cm range. The area to the southwest of the dehydration unit was scraped about an inch deep to remove the visually impacted soil. The area under the reboiler was excavated about 8 inches deep to remove the visually impacted soil. Conductivity of the finished excavation area according to Penn E and R was 500-1200 uS/cm. EQT was planning on having Penn E and R collect confirmatory samples for the cleanup of the spill.On April 14, 2023, EQT ARO LLC provided the DEP a revision on the estimated amount spilled at the dehydration unit to approximately 15-20 gallons. The estimation was revised based on the amount of soil that was excavated and EQT observation of their midstream system monitoring equipment indicating increased moisture content showing some of the release went into the pipeline. The spilling of triethylene glycol and production fluid outside of containment to the well pad surface is a violation of Clean Streams Law Section 402(b), Chapter 78a.56(a), and Solid Waste ManagementAct Section 301. These violations have been immediately corrected.

Comments: The Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted a follow-up inspection of Blackhill Energy's (Blackhill) Jackson A well site located in Springfield Township, Bradford County on 4/10/2023 at 1525 hours. The weather was 67 degrees with clear skies. The inspection was conducted to evaluate remedial activities that were conducted after a release that occurred on 4/6/2023.Moody and Associates Inc. (Moody's)(Environmental consultant) was onsite during my inspection and have been conducting field screenings for Blackhill. Since the release that occurred on 4/6/2023, Blackhill has had the entire southern stormwater conveyance channel excavated (photos #2, 3 and 4). Blackhill reported that soil readings in the channel were now field measured below 1.0mS/cm. Excavation points on both sides of the access road culvert are now acting as sumps for the collection of residual fluids. A water truck was stationed at these points today, recovering any collected fluids. The pad surface area that was determined to be impacted by the release has been excavated as much as possible (photos #6 and 7). Blackhill explained that collected fluids shown in photo #7 are also being recovered. Fluid in this area, which is located right next to the initial release point, was field measured at ~17.8mS/cm today. Blackhill reported that equipment will be brought in on either 4/11/2023 or 4/12/2023 to move the produced water tanks and associated secondary containment structure in order to excavate beneath them. The impacted stormwater basin has been emptied to where just a few puddles remain (photo #1). All water collected from the basin was stored in tanks shown in photo #9 and continues to be trucked offsite for disposal or reuse. I field measured a small puddle near the stormwater channel entry point of the basin which returned a reading of ~1.75mS/cm. All impacted materials that have been recovered are stored in lined and covered waste containers which are held on secondary containment (photo #8). All violations associated with the releases from 1/2/2023 and from 4/6/2023 remain outstanding at this time against API #015-23733. I departed the site at 1620 hours.As a follow-up to the violations cited on 4/6/2023, the DEP requests a summary of the quantity of fluids collected in regards to the produced water release, including the stormwater basin, and where the water was transported after collection. properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: SCORPIO ENERGY INC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 9/02/2026
Violation Code: 102.22(b)1 - SITE STABILIZATION – TEMPORARY STABILIZATION – Permitee failed to temporarily stabilize the site to protect it from accelerated erosion and sedimentation where cessation of earth disturbance activities exceeded 4 days.
Violation ID: 8287774
Permit API: 053-31161
Unconventional: No
County: Forest
Municipality: Howe Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 9/02/2026
Comments: This site is undergoing construction for the development of a conventional well. The drilling permit and E and S Plan are posted at the entrance of the location. There was no activity on the location at the time of this inspection. The template for the site and access road has been completed. The gathering lines for this well have been buried within the template of the road. Stone has not yet been applied to any portion of the road or well site. The E and S Plan that was prepared for this site is inadequate as it does not account for all surface waters of the Commonwealth that converge with the earth disturbance associated with the construction of this well site and the access road that leads to it. In addition, the site and access road have been excavated significantly below the natural grade, therefore, watercourses that were likely below the surface prior to construction are now present at the surface and are not accounted for in the E and S Plan. Due to the insufficient plan and construction practices, the BMPs that have been installed are insufficient and are promoting stormwater to become concentrated and directed into waters of the Commonwealth. Numerous waters of the Commonwealth are also being removed from their natural channel and redirected.The ditches along the access road do not consist of a durable material, nor have they been stabilized to account for the flow of water running through them and have become significantly eroded due to the volume and velocity of stormwater and surface water. Aside from the lack of stabilization measures in the ditch, the roadside banks and perimeter of the location (that do not appear to require any additional excavation) have also not yet been stabilized. No perimeter BMPs (such as silt sock) have been installed for minimizing the amount of sediment leaving the un-stabilized areas of earth disturbance. The culverts that have been installed at the intermittent streams have been poorly installed. There is excessive excavation at the inlets and outlets of these water features resulting in sediment entering the stream channels. The E and S Plan does not account for headwall protection at these culverts, therefore, the disturbed earth near the inlets and outlets is vulnerable to scouring and erosion into the water channel. Improper installation and the lack of energy dissipators at the outlets of the installed cross-pipes that are conveying stormwater is resulting in scouring at the outlets of these culverts and increasing the amount of accelerated erosion and sedimentation. Since no stone has been placed on the road, recent traffic on the road template after rain events has caused the template to become soft and appreciably rutted in spots. This has allowed stormwater, and in some areas, the flow from a watercourse to flow onto the road template. As a result of these deficiencies, there has been accelerated erosion across the earth disturbance associated with the construction of the access road and well site. Significant amounts of sediment have discharged into and remain accumulated in spring seeps and unnamed tributary of Hastings Run.In addition to the E and S deficiencies, due to the abundance of shallow ground water at the site, the use of pits for temporary containment or permanent encapsulation of cuttings or any residual waste from this well in a pit would not satisfy the requirements outlined in Chapter 78.56(a)(8), unless Scorpio Energy can demonstrate otherwise to the Department in advance of lining the pit.The deficiencies noted above also apply to the first well location (Well Site 56) and the access road getting to that site. Corrective action should be applied to both sites in order to remediate the noted violations and to return to compliance.

The E and S Plan that was prepared for this site is inadequate as it does not account for all surface waters of the Commonwealth that converge with the earth disturbance associated with the construction of this well site and the access road that leads to it. In addition, the site and access road have been excavated significantly below the natural grade, therefore, watercourses that were likely below the surface prior to construction are now present at the surface and are not accounted for in the E and S Plan. Due to the insufficient plan and construction practices, the BMPs that have been installed are insufficient and are promoting stormwater to become concentrated and directed into waters of the Commonwealth. Numerous waters of the Commonwealth are also being removed from their natural channel and redirected.The ditches along the access road do not consist of a durable material, nor have they been stabilized to account for the flow of water running through them and have become significantly eroded due to the volume and velocity of stormwater and surface water. Aside from the lack of stabilization measures in the ditch, the roadside banks and perimeter of the location (that do not appear to require any additional excavation) have also not yet been stabilized. No perimeter BMPs (such as silt sock) have been installed for minimizing the amount of sediment leaving the un-stabilized areas of earth disturbance. The culverts that have been installed at the intermittent streams have been poorly installed. There is excessive excavation at the inlets and outlets of these water features resulting in sediment entering the stream channels. The E and S Plan does not account for headwall protection at these culverts, therefore, the disturbed earth near the inlets and outlets is vulnerable to scouring and erosion into the water channel. Improper installation and the lack of energy dissipators at the outlets of the installed cross-pipes that are conveying stormwater is resulting in scouring at the outlets of these culverts and increasing the amount of accelerated erosion and sedimentation. Since no stone has been placed on the road, recent traffic on the road template after rain events has caused the template to become soft and appreciably rutted in spots. This has allowed stormwater, and in some areas, the flow from a watercourse to flow onto the road template. As a result of these deficiencies, there has been accelerated erosion across the earth disturbance associated with the construction of the access road and well site. Significant amounts of sediment have discharged into and remain accumulated in spring seeps and unnamed tributary of Hastings Run.In addition to the E and S deficiencies, due to the abundance of shallow ground water at the site, the use of pits for temporary containment or permanent encapsulation of cuttings or any residual waste from this well in a pit would not satisfy the requirements outlined in Chapter 78.56(a)(8), unless Scorpio Energy can demonstrate otherwise to the Department in advance of lining the pit.The deficiencies noted above also apply to the first well location (Well Site 56) and the access road getting to that site. Corrective action should be applied to both sites in order to remediate the noted violations and to return to compliance.

SWMA 302(A) - DISPOSAL, PROCESSING AND STORAGE OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person disposed, processed, stored, or permitted the disposal, processing or storage of residual waste in a manner which is contrary to the rules and regulations of DEP or to any permit or to the terms or conditions of any permit or any order issued by DEP.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: PENNHILLS RESOURCES LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 3/15/2022
Violation Code: SWMA 302(A) - DISPOSAL, PROCESSING AND STORAGE OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person disposed, processed, stored, or permitted the disposal, processing or storage of residual waste in a manner which is contrary to the rules and regulations of DEP or to any permit or to the terms or conditions of any permit or any order issued by DEP.
Violation ID: 948070
Permit API: 083-49666
Unconventional: No
County: McKean
Municipality: Hamilton Twp
Inspection Type: Complaint Inspection
Inspection Date: 3/15/2022
Comments: This inspection was performed following a report of an oil and gas leak in the vicinity of Chappel Fork near the road crossing of RT 321 (CTS #362745). At the time of the report to DEP, I spoke to the complainant and determined the location to begin searching. I contacted Pennhills Resources as they have wells in the immediate vicinity, and we agreed to meet on site to look. After beginning at Rt 321 we headed east until we found some oil collected in a low spot. It appears as though a line has burst with some gas pressure on the line, causing oil and gas to bubble to the surface. The oil then flowed south and into a low swale, where the majority of it collected. Some crude then flowed through into a channel formed by the collection of two spring runs, and toward the main branch of Chappel Fork. Oil was collecting behind ice pockets and in between leaves and dead vegetation for approximately 200 feet. A small amount of sheen was noted in Chappel Fork, but no free product. Approximately 15-20 barrels of oil was emitted from the line in total. Another small area nearer to the creek when following the line was noted to contain some basic sediment and paraffin at the surface and under a hemlock tree; it is uncertain if this is another leak site or simply product following the line. Pennhills immediately moved to contain the spill with booms in the back channel, and then brought a mini excavator to site to dig up the line and slow the leak. The 2" line was uncovered and a band placed on the line, which was broken on the bottom. It was determined that the old access past well 9A could be used to mobilize equipment and some brush was removed to make for better access. A vac truck was brought to site to collect any free product available, which was able to get a large amount on the first load. It was determined the evening of 3/15 that the line belonged to Pennhills, who will be continuing to clean up the oil and soil until clean. The operator built two underflow dams to contain any free product flowing down the channel with melting ice starting to give way. Followup inspection will be performed as necessary.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 6/30/2025 to EQT ARO LLC in Plunketts Creek Township, Lycoming county. SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP. properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 6/30/2025
Violation Code: SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP. Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 8239849
Permit API: 081-21995
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: Plunketts Creek Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 6/30/2025
Comments: Arrived onsite on 6/30/25 in response to a reported release of at least 5 gallons of produced fluid. The release occurred near the evaporator units on the eastern side of the pad and may have been the result of a faulty inlet valve on the evaporators. Tobias Machine and Welding, Penn E and R, and Rick Hall (EQT) were onsite to screen and assess the extent of the release. There were two stains visible on the pad (Photos 1 and 2). The larger stain was approximately 13' by 6' and the smaller stain was approximately 4' by 1'. There was no visible fluid off the pad surface but soil conductivity readings were taken. The soil below the staining between the toe of the pad slope and about halfway to the treeline (Photos 3, 4, and 5) had conductivities over 4.00 millisiemens per centimeter (mS/cm). Closer to the trees the soil conductivity dropped to around 2.2 mS/cm. Inside the woods the conductivity ranged between 0.05 mS/cm to 0.21 mS/cm.I returned on 7/2/25 to check on the progress of the remediation. The impacted area had been scraped (Photos 6, 7, and 8). Soil conductivity was again checked. Conductivities outside the scraped area ranged from 0.20 mS/cm to 0.40 mS/cm. There were a few localized areas within the work area that ranged between 1.74 mS/cm and 3.17 mS/cm. These readings were generally shallow and appeared where there were scrape marks from the excavation. Tobias was going to continue removing soil from these areas as they were finishing the bulk of the remediation. The excavated area was roughly 50' from the pad to the treeline and about 20' to 30' across.During a phone call with Rick Hall (EQT) on 7/3/25, it was determined that the remediated area had been backfilled and stabilized. There were 7 dumpsters of impacted soil that were in the process of being disposed of. EQT also indicated that remediation under Act 2 would be pursued and Penn E and R already collected the necessary confirmation samples.The result of this inspection is Violations Noted for CSL 402(b), SWMA 301, and 78a56(a). The violations may be closed after the completion of Act 2 remediation.

Comments: On 2/4/2026, DEP representative John Rogers conducted a drilling/alteration inspection at the Seneca Resource's Taft 851 well site located in Middlebury Township, Tioga County. It was 10 degrees and mostly clear when I arrived on location. Due to frozen conditions, conductivity readings were not taken during this inspection.When I arrived at the active north pad, I met with Seneca's Mark McCormick who described current operations as follows. Drilling to total depth has been completed on eight new gas wells at the site. Crews were on site, prepping for upcoming stimulation operations on the eight wells. Frac equipment was being mobilized to the location. Fracking has not commenced but is expected to start on 2/12/2026 depending on when the crew finishes on the DCNR 007 L Pad and depending on weather. Mark expects stimulation activities on the eight wells to be completed by the end of June 2026. In addition to 28 frac tanks that were stationed on the west side of the pad during previous operations, four pump down frac tanks, two gas buster frac tanks and five working frac tanks have been staged on the pad. Five wells have been completed at the site and were staged for production. Three sand separators remain near the wells but have been disconnected.Three sediment traps and one sediment basin have been installed on site and along the access road. They have not been converted to PCSM BMPs yet. Sediment trap 3 and the sediment basin did have standing water/ice. Temporary compost filter socks remain installed throughout the site. The original south pad and access road for the Taft 851 1V well have been returned to original grade.Violations are still outstanding for inspection ID 3846665 and ID 3855651 for puddles of water with elevated conductance discovered on the pad surface and in the sediment basin during completion operations.The DEP recommends that Seneca continues to monitor the conditions on the pad surface and the sediment basin and remove elevated conductance fluids and soils as discovered. Prevent elevated conductance fluids from leaving the facility and causing pollution to the waters of the Commonwealth. I left the site at 0930 hours.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 11/16/2022 to CHESAPEAKE APPALACHIA LLC in Asylum Twp, Bradford county. CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: CHESAPEAKE APPALACHIA LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 11/16/2022
Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 976074
Permit API: 015-23708
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Asylum Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 11/16/2022
Comments: On 11/16/2022, DEP representative John Rogers conducted an incident/response to accident or event inspection at the Chesapeake Hopson well site. This inspection is in response to Complaint Id 368309 for one barrel of brine water spilled outside of secondary containment from a frac tank on the site.Prior to my arrival, Chesapeake's Danielle Schaad informed me that the frac tank would be to the right when arriving on site and was stationed in secondary containment by itself. She said that the location of the leak in the frac tank and in the secondary containment was unknown but high conductance water was discovered outside of secondary containment on the pad surface. She said that the fluid was brine water from the produced water tank. She reported that the tank and secondary containment had been emptied and the puddle vacuumed up. She said that the tank was being removed from location and that Cresson Environmental would be onsite on 11/17/2022. It was 40 degrees and overcast when I arrived on location. Heavy snowfall had impacted the region in the last 24 hours and was melting with the pad being mostly clear of snow. A skid steer and a vac truck had just arrived on location and were setting up next to a frac tank in the northeast corner of the site. The frac tank was still connected to the 1HC gas well GPU. A crew was working on disconnecting it from the GPU. A vac box was located south of the frac tank. I field tested various water puddles in close proximity to the frac tank for conductance using an Oakton PCTS 50 with an upper limit of 20.0 mS with the following results: 40'x 40' water puddle on the south west corner of the frac tank secondary containment field tested at 0.77 mS.5' x 8' water puddle outside the southeast corner of the vac box field tested at 14.43 mS.20' x 20' water puddle southeast of the frac tank secondary containment was over 20.0 mS.15 x 30' water puddle east of the frac tank secondary containment was over 20.0 mS.6' x 20' water puddle northeast of the frac tank secondary containment field tested at 3.53 mS.12' x 40' water puddle on the east edge of the site above the recently excavated fill slope field tested at 2.33 mS.Water below the rocked section of the fill slope field tested at 1.20 mS. Water in the south end of infiltration area 1 field tested at 1.40 mS.Other water puddles on the pad surface field tested at 0.8 mS or less.There were ten wells staged for production. All wells were tagged with API/well permit numbers. No bubbling within the cellars was observed. A rainbow sheen was witnessed in the Hopson 101HC, 22HC, 4HC and 5H well cellars. Six of the GPUs and the production tank had secondary containment. There were six frac tanks and one gas buster staged in secondary containment on the west side of location. While on site the frac tank with the suspected leak and the secondary containment were removed from location. Water puddles adjacent to the frac tank location were vacuumed up. Joe Button discussed that an excavator will be brought to location along with Creston Environmental to conduct cleanup operations at 0800 hrs on 11/17/2022. This spill constitutes violations of these three regulations; 78a 56[a), SWMA 301, and CSL 402(b)The DEP recommends pursuing Act 2 remediation in accordance with 78a 66(c)The department also recommends removing the water from and cleaning the well cellars noted for having sheens; the Hopson 101HC, 22HC, 4HC and 5H well cellars.Violations are still outstanding for inspection ID 3406647 for high conductance fluid escaping from damaged containment during well stimulation activities with an unknown volume impacting the pad surface.I left the site at 1400 hours.

properties.content:
Report Details

Permit API: 015-21165
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford

Inspection Type: Plugging(Includes Plugged/Mined Through)
Inspection Date: 5/27/2026
Comments: At time of inspection: On site for a post-plugging inspection of the Oberkamper 1H (015-21165) well to check for gas at a plugged well. Met with EOG rep. Russel Juart. Russ confirmed all valves were open. The cellar was full of water and there was no bubbling noticed. All vents and production casing were open and vented. A Remote Methane Leak Detector (RMLD) was used to check the ambient air at the well for methane. An Altair 5x gas meter was used for further confirmation. There was no gas detected at the well. There were no obvious concerns noticed. Operator may proceed with installation of tacking on monument/vent marker. Please include a picture of installed monument/vent marker, prior to burial, and an as plugged wellbore schematic with the submission of the Certificate of Well Plugging for this well. There are outstanding violations 78a81(a)2, 78a73(b), 78a85(a)5 and 78a86 on this well from 7/5/2019 that appears to have been addressed through plugging operations. There were no new violations noted during this inspection. These violations will be closed upon receipt of the plugging certificate.

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: EQUITRANS LP

Violation Date: 1/21/2021
Violation Code: 78.91(a) - PLUGGING - GENERAL PROVISIONS - Upon abandoning a well, the owner or operator failed to plug the well to stop the vertical flow of fluids or gas within the well bore under 25 Pa. Code §§ 78.92—78.98 or an approved alternate method.
Violation ID: 905606
Permit API: 059-20004
Unconventional: No
County: Greene
Municipality: Morgan Twp
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 1/21/2021
Comments: On January 21, 2021, the Department performed an inspection of the Equitrans John Buckingham 1 well site. Present at time of inspection was the landowner's son Nathan Spitznoggle. The site is located in Morgan Twp., Greene County. The inspection was a followup inspection of the site related to a violation issued on 11/20/19 and 6/16/2020. The Department was notified by the operator on 11/20/19 of gas observations in the soil around the John H Buckingham plugged storage well. The permit number is affixed to the monument. The monument indicates that the well was plugged on 11/21/2008. The Department collected gas readings from the slam bar holes using a Bascom Turner 611 EGA meter. Gas readings were collected at ground surface. A peak reading of 1100 PPM gas was detected in slam bar holes closest to the monument on the northeast side of the monument. The Department did not detect a combustible atmosphere in the ambient air around the well. The plugged storage well is approximately 20' southwest of a mobile home. The mobile home was not occupied at the time of the inspection. Based on the observations around the plugged well, the operator, upon abandoning the well, failed to plug the well to stop the vertical flow of gas within the well bore. The violation of Chapter 78a.91(a) issued for failing to plug a well to stop the vertical flow of fluids or gas within the well bore is still outstanding. The violation issued for failing to submit a certificate of plugging to the Department within 30 days after the well has been plugged has been remediated.

Comments: On 09/17/2025, an incident inspection was conducted at the Harden Farms Well Site following receipt of an incident report that was submitted to the Department on 09/17/2025 at 12:17 (CTS 392314).It was reported that 10 gallons of biocide material was spilled on site at 12:00, 09/17/2025. No waterways were affected. It was also reported that a clean up crew (SPSI) was on site.I called the EQT representative who reported the spill, Lance Witters, for information. I noted that SPSI arrived after I did, and I requested the Safety Data Sheet (SDS) to be sent to me. It was described to me that the material spilled was a Multi-Chem biocide. The cause of the release was that a hose back pressured, biocide flowed back to the tank, and the tank overflowed. It was estimated that 10 gallons spilled.SPSI had not began remediation and was not on the pad when I arrived. No personal were on the pad upon my arrival.The following was observed:The contaminated area was adjacent to the gas production units (GPUs). It was unknown if any production fluid was present in addition to the biocide spilled; no elevated conductivity was observed. No remediation had begun and SPSI was not on the pad when I arrived on the pad. SPSI arrived to the site after the Department (Photo 1). An extremely strong odor was experienced on site in the vicinity of the contaminated area.SPSI then arrived on the pad and had not begun remediation while I was on site. The impacted area was located between the well heads and the GPUs. The impacted area appeared wet with small sections of pooled fluid (Photos 2-5).I asked SPSI if they had the SDS, and they did not. The SDS was not located on site with the site documents in the mailboxes. I was able to locate a Control and Disposal Plan and the Site Specific Safety and Environmental Plan and Policy. I was not able to locate any information related to the Multi-Chem biocide (Photos 6-9). I also did not find a Preparedness, Prevention, and Contingency Plan (PPC) on site. The SDSs are required to be on site. The PPC Plan is also required to be on site during drilling or completion activities, however the well operator shall prepare and develop a site specific PPC plan prior to storing, using, or generating regulated substances to, on or from a well site.The Act 9 sign was at the site entrance (Photo 10).The Department requests a description of the activities that were being carried out that resulted in a spill.Due to the SDS not present on site, a PPC Plan not on site, failure to control regulated fluids with a release to the ground, and failure to use secondary containment, violations of 78a.54, 78a55(a), 78a55(b), 78a55(i)5iD, SWMA 301, 91.34(a), and 78a64a(b) are being issued.
